claimed_invariant: Deployment model identity is the cleaned canonical quark code and is independent of visible display text. A qualified name is the ordered ancestor quark-code path joined by Plasma's separator. Only at SVG group metadata serialization does UGroup.fix replace each character outside ASCII word characters, space, and hyphen with a dot; hierarchy separators and punctuation therefore project uniformly while dots, underscores, spaces, and hyphens survive.
causal_divergence: Rust stores canonical id and visible label but then discards that distinction in metadata helpers: own_qname and qualified_name recompute label_to_id to guess whether an alias existed, qname_label_segment replaces only colons, and deployment_qnames repeats the same heuristic. The quoted display-first parser also limits aliases to word characters, so dotted canonical codes are truncated before rendering. Thus punctuation-bearing no-alias identities remain raw and explicit dotted aliases lose suffixes. Geometry and paint-order differences in one predecessor input are secondary consequences of corrupted model identity and ownership.
planned_model_change: Treat DeploymentNode.id as the sole canonical quark segment, preserve broad explicit container aliases in the parser, build qualified paths from parent ownership plus canonical segments, and apply one shared UGroup.fix-compatible helper at the metadata boundary. Remove label-derived identity heuristics from every deployment qualified-name path while leaving visible labels untouched. Use that same projected map for oracle lookup, no-oracle layout records, clusters, leaves, and metadata consumers.
perturbation_axes: identity form: quoted no-alias versus explicit display-first alias versus bare canonical code
punctuation class: colon, slash, parentheses, dot, underscore, hyphen, space, and non-ASCII code points
ownership depth: root, one-level container, and nested container paths
display independence: renamed display with stable alias and stable display with changed alias
consumer: cluster metadata, leaf metadata, links, and no-oracle layout lookup
acceptance: Both preserved Java-success predecessor inputs produce byte-level no-oracle parity without changing visible labels to fit metadata.
Focused parser and renderer tests prove canonical/display separation, ancestor path construction, and the exact UGroup.fix ASCII projection boundary.
